name: Abramelin Oil
description: The holy anointing oil of The Book of Abramelin, a 15th-century grimoire, adapted from the Exodus recipe of myrrh, cinnamon and sweet calamus. Ceremonial magicians from Mathers to Crowley used it to consecrate tools, altars and themselves before high ritual. This skin-safe version keeps the classic triad but leans on myrrh and galangal-style warmth from ginger, with cinnamon present only as a whisper.

ingredients.item: Jojoba or sweet almond carrier oil

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Drop the myrrh tear and cinnamon chip into the empty bottle as the 'bones' of the oil.
Add the essential oils one at a time in the order listed, starting with myrrh, so the base note anchors the blend.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Anoint the brow, crown and palms before ritual, trace a cross or pentagram on wands, chalices and altar cloths to consecrate them, and dress white or gold candles from the center outward for spiritual elevation.
chant: Oil of the sages, sweet and old, myrrh and fire, a holy gold; whatsoever you shall touch, be consecrated, blessed as such.
intention: I consecrate myself and my tools to the highest work of spirit.
timing: Full moon or Sunday at dawn, in the hour of the Sun.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2.5% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Cinnamon leaf oil is a strong skin sensitizer, so keep to the drops given and never substitute cinnamon bark or cassia oil, which are far harsher; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
interactions: Cinnamon leaf oil is rich in eugenol, which has antiplatelet effects; if you take warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel or other blood thinners, have a bleeding disorder or have surgery coming up, use this blend sparingly or not at all.
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains cinnamon oil, which is especially risky for cats.

name: Florida Water-Style Oil
description: Florida Water is a 19th-century American cologne whose bright citrus and spice made it a staple of hoodoo, Spiritualism and Caribbean traditions for cleansing and pleasing the spirits. Rather than an alcohol cologne, this is an oil version of its bouquet: bergamot, orange, lemon, lavender and a breath of clove. Use it wherever you want a fresh, spirit-friendly cleansing scent that lingers.

ingredients.item: Fractionated coconut or jojoba carrier oil

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the dried orange peel strip in the empty bottle.
Add the citrus oils first, then lavender, then the single drop of clove.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Rub a drop between your palms and sweep your aura from head to foot after crowded places, dress white candles for spirit offerings, and anoint door frames and windowsills to keep the house bright and clear.
chant: Bright as the morning, sweet as the sea, wash every shadow away from me.
intention: I am refreshed, cleansed and welcome to good spirits.
timing: Any day; Monday or the waxing moon for spirit offerings.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2.3% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Clove bud oil is a strong skin sensitizer, so keep to the drops given and never substitute cinnamon bark or cassia oil, which are far harsher; cold-pressed lemon oil is phototoxic above about 2% on skin (the IFRA limit); this blend stays well below that, so do not add extra lemon or other cold-pressed citrus, and if you do, keep anointed skin out of sun and tanning beds for 12 hours; steam-distilled lemon is not phototoxic; use only bergamot labeled FCF (bergaptene-free), because ordinary bergamot can cause severe sunburn-like blistering. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
interactions: Clove oil is rich in eugenol, which has antiplatelet effects; if you take warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel or other blood thinners, have a bleeding disorder or have surgery coming up, use this blend sparingly or not at all.
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains citrus and clove oils, which are especially risky for cats.

name: Four Thieves Oil
description: Named for the legend of plague-era thieves who robbed the sick yet stayed well thanks to an herbal vinegar, the formula has become a byword for protection against illness and ill will. In hoodoo it doubles as a protection and enemy-repelling oil. This blend balances clove, cinnamon, lemon, eucalyptus and rosemary at a safe dilution.
steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Slip the dried rosemary sprig into the empty bottle.
Add lemon, rosemary and eucalyptus first, then clove and the single drop of cinnamon leaf.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Anoint the soles of your shoes and your wrists before entering a hostile place, dress black or white candles for protection of the household, or dab on doorknobs and thresholds to keep out illness and troublemakers.
chant: Four who walked where sickness lay, kept their health by night and day; by clove and lemon, rosemary, no harm nor ill shall come to me.
intention: I am protected in body and spirit, and no ill can take hold of me.
timing: Saturday or the waning moon.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2.5% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Cinnamon leaf and clove bud oils are strong skin sensitizers, so keep to the drops given and never substitute cinnamon bark or cassia oil, which are far harsher; cold-pressed lemon oil is phototoxic above about 2% on skin (the IFRA limit); this blend stays well below that, so do not add extra lemon or other cold-pressed citrus, and if you do, keep anointed skin out of sun and tanning beds for 12 hours; steam-distilled lemon is not phototoxic; eucalyptus and rosemary oils must never be used on or near the face of infants and young children, and people with epilepsy should avoid this blend; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
interactions: Clove and cinnamon leaf oils are rich in eugenol, which has antiplatelet effects; if you take warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel or other blood thinners, have a bleeding disorder or have surgery coming up, use this blend sparingly or not at all.
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains citrus, eucalyptus, cinnamon and clove oils, which are especially risky for cats.

name: Fiery Wall of Protection Oil
description: A classic hoodoo formula that throws up a ring of spiritual fire around the worker, built on dragon's blood resin, frankincense, myrrh and hot spice. It is used when you feel under attack, cursed, or simply exposed. This version gets its fire from infused resin and ginger rather than heavy amounts of skin-burning oils.
steps: Warm the carrier oil with the powdered dragon's blood in a double boiler on the lowest heat for 1 hour, stirring now and then; it will tint the oil red.
Cool, then strain through a coffee filter into a cleansed 1 oz glass bottle.
Add the pinch of salt, then the frankincense, myrrh, ginger and the single drop of cinnamon leaf, and the vitamin E.
Roll the bottle between your palms while visualizing a ring of flame encircling you.
Speak the chant, label, and rest it in the dark for 3 days before use.
howToUse: Dress red or white candles from base to wick and set them at the four corners of your home, anoint your heart and the back of your neck before going out, and trace a circle of oil around photos of loved ones you wish to shield.
chant: Wall of fire, rise and stand, ring me round on every hand; what is sent to do me harm, burns to ash against this charm.
intention: A wall of holy fire surrounds me and nothing harmful can pass.
timing: Tuesday or Sunday; waxing to full moon.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2.2% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Cinnamon leaf oil is a strong skin sensitizer, so keep to the drops given and never substitute cinnamon bark or cassia oil, which are far harsher; dragon's blood stains skin and fabric red, and resin oils should be warmed only in a double boiler, never over direct flame or unattended; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. Buy only plant-resin dragon's blood (Daemonorops or Dracaena); the name is also used for other red substances, including toxic mercury sulfide (cinnabar), which must never be burned or put on skin. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
interactions: Cinnamon leaf oil is rich in eugenol, which has antiplatelet effects; if you take warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel or other blood thinners, have a bleeding disorder or have surgery coming up, use this blend sparingly or not at all.
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains cinnamon oil, which is especially risky for cats.

name: Van Van Oil
description: Van Van is perhaps the most famous New Orleans conjure oil, built on the lemony grasses of Southeast Asia: lemongrass, citronella, palmarosa, gingergrass and vetiver. It is an all-purpose luck, cleansing and road-clearing oil that also 'powers up' charms, lodestones and mojo bags. A pinch of pyrite or a piece of lemongrass in the bottle is traditional.

ingredients.item: Sweet almond or grapeseed carrier oil

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the dried lemongrass piece and the pyrite chip into the empty bottle.
Add lemongrass, citronella, palmarosa and finally vetiver as the grounding base.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Dress green, yellow or white candles for luck and clearing, anoint amulets, lodestones and mojo bags to empower them, add a few drops to a floor wash (scrubbing toward the front door), or wear a dab on the wrists when you need things to break your way.
chant: Van Van, clear the way, bring me luck by night and day; sweep the bad and call the good, open roads as roads all should.
intention: I clear away what blocks me and draw good luck to every step.
timing: New moon or Thursday; any time you need a fresh start.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2.2% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Lemongrass is a skin sensitizer, so use no more than about 4 drops per ounce; sweet almond oil can affect people with tree nut allergies, so use jojoba or sunflower instead if that applies. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds.

name: Road Opener Oil
description: Road Opener oil draws on the energy of Elegua and Papa Legba, guardians of crossroads, to remove obstacles and open the way to new opportunities. It is used before job hunts, moves, new ventures or when everything feels stuck. Its bright citrus top notes are grounded with vetiver and a key or a sprig of Devil's Shoestring.

ingredients.item: Allspice essential oil (no more than 1 drop; optional)

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Drop the small key and the Devil's Shoestring root piece into the bottle to unlock and trip up obstacles.
Add the essential oils in order: citrus and grass, then peppermint, then vetiver and allspice.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Dress orange or white candles and burn them at a crossroads altar or windowsill, anoint the soles of your shoes before interviews or applications, and touch a drop to door handles, keys and your car's steering wheel to open the way.
chant: Keeper of the crossroads, turn the key, open every road for me; what is stuck now comes undone, I walk forward toward the sun.
intention: Every road before me opens and obstacles fall away.
timing: Monday or Wednesday, new to waxing moon.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2.2% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Allspice oil is high in eugenol and irritating, with a skin maximum of about 0.15%, so one drop in 30 ml is already at the limit: never add more, and leave it out for sensitive skin; lemongrass is a skin sensitizer, so use no more than about 4 drops per ounce; peppermint oil must never be used on or near the face of infants and young children, and people with epilepsy should avoid this blend. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
interactions: Allspice oil is rich in eugenol, which has antiplatelet effects; if you take warfarin, aspirin, clopidogrel or other blood thinners, have a bleeding disorder or have surgery coming up, use this blend sparingly or not at all.
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains citrus and peppermint oils, which are especially risky for cats.

name: Come to Me Oil
description: A traditional hoodoo love-drawing oil worn to attract a new lover or to call a specific person closer. Rose and jasmine form the heart of the scent, with a touch of lavender and vanilla for sweetness. It is gentle in intent: it invites, rather than forces.
steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the rose buds and a pinch of damiana into the bottle.
Add the florals first, then lavender, then vanilla.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Wear on the pulse points and over the heart when you will see the one you desire, dress red or pink figure candles for love-drawing, and anoint love letters or the corners of a photograph.
chant: Rose and jasmine, honey sweet, guide my love to me to meet; heart to heart and hand to hand, come to me by love's command.
intention: I draw a loving, willing partner toward me.
timing: Friday in the hour of Venus, waxing moon.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.

name: Money Drawing Oil
description: A cornerstone of hoodoo money work, used to draw steady cash and opportunity. Green and spicy, it combines basil, patchouli and cinnamon's warmth with bayberry tradition and a few cinquefoil leaves, the 'five-finger grass' that grasps whatever you seek. Add a coin or pyrite to the bottle for extra pull.

ingredients.item: Sunflower or sweet almond carrier oil

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the cinquefoil, allspice berries and coin into the bottle.
Add patchouli, basil, orange and finally the single drop of cinnamon leaf.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.
howToUse: Dress green candles from wick to base to draw money toward you, anoint the corners of your wallet, cash register or business cards, rub a drop on your palms before negotiations, and anoint the first dollar you earn each day.
chant: Money come and money stay, money grow from day to day; green and gold flow into me, as I will, so mote it be.
intention: Money flows to me easily and abundantly.
timing: Thursday or Sunday, waxing moon.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2.2% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.

name: Crown of Success Oil
description: A hoodoo formula for mastery, recognition and achievement, worn before exams, auditions, promotions and competitions. Its royal ingredients are frankincense, sandalwood and bay laurel, ruled by the Sun, with a chip of High John the Conqueror root for unstoppable will.

ingredients.item: High John the Conqueror root chip

chant: Crown of gold upon my head, wisdom shine where I am led; laurel, sandal, frankincense, success is mine in every sense.
intention: I rise to mastery and am recognized for my gifts.
timing: Sunday in the hour of the Sun, waxing moon.

Bay laurel oil can sensitize skin, so keep to the drops given. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.

name: Uncrossing Oil
description: Uncrossing oil removes jinxes, crossed conditions and spiritual heaviness, whether sent by another or self-inflicted. Traditional formulas lean on hyssop, the biblical purifier, with agrimony to return harm to its sender and the sharp, clearing scent of lemon and eucalyptus.

ingredients.item: Hyssop essential oil (Hyssopus officinalis var. decumbens)

steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Place the hyssop, agrimony and salt into the bottle.
Add the essential oils, lemon first and frankincense last.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.

chant: What was crossed is now made straight, every curse dissolves its weight; hyssop, wash and make me clean, uncrossed, unbound, and free, serene.
intention: Every crossing on me is lifted and I walk free and clear.
timing: Waning moon, Saturday.

name: Peaceful Home Oil
description: A soothing hoodoo and folk formula used to calm quarrels, ease tension between housemates and keep a gentle atmosphere at home. Lavender, chamomile and rose are classic peacemakers, with a touch of sweet orange for cheer.
steps: Cleanse a 1 oz (30 ml) amber or cobalt glass bottle by rinsing it with salt water and passing it through incense smoke, then dry it completely.
Add the lavender buds to the bottle.
Blend in lavender, chamomile, orange and rose in that order.
Fill the bottle almost to the shoulder with the carrier oil, leaving room to swirl, and add the vitamin E to slow rancidity.
Cap and roll the bottle gently between your palms (do not shake) for a few minutes while holding your intention firmly in mind.
Speak the chant over the bottle, label it with the name and date, and let it rest in a dark cupboard for at least 3 days (ideally one full moon cycle) so the scents marry.

chant: Peace within these walls abide, calm and kindness, side by side; anger fade and quarrel cease, fill this home with gentle peace.
intention: My home is filled with peace, harmony and kindness.
timing: Monday or Friday, waxing or full moon.
caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. name: Psychic Vision Oil
description: An oil for opening the inner eye before divination, scrying or tarot. Mugwort, the classic seer's herb, is infused into the carrier, then brightened with clary sage, lemongrass and a resinous base of sandalwood.
steps: Place the dried mugwort in a clean jar and cover with the carrier oil; set in a sunny-to-moonlit window for 2 weeks, shaking daily (or warm gently in a double boiler for 2 hours).
Strain through cheesecloth into a cleansed 1 oz bottle, squeezing the herb well.
Add sandalwood, clary sage, lemongrass and the drop of star anise, then the vitamin E.
Roll between your palms while visualizing an eye of light opening on your brow.
Speak the chant and rest the oil on your altar under the full moon before first use.
howToUse: Anoint the third eye (between the brows) and temples before readings, dress purple or silver candles beside your scrying bowl, and wipe a drop on tarot boxes, pendulums and crystal balls.
chant: Veil of mist, now draw aside, open the eye where truths abide; mugwort, moon and silver light, grant me vision, grant me sight.

name: Dragon's Blood Power Oil
description: Dragon's blood resin from Daemonorops and Dracaena trees has been prized since antiquity as a pigment, medicine and magical power-booster. This oil is a resin infusion warmed with cinnamon and patchouli and is added to any working to amplify it, or used alone for protection and personal power.
steps: Combine the crushed resin and carrier oil in a double boiler and warm on low heat for 1 to 2 hours, stirring until the oil is deep red.
Cool and decant into a cleansed 1 oz bottle, leaving a few resin pieces at the bottom.
Add patchouli, frankincense, orange and the drop of cinnamon leaf, plus the vitamin E.
Roll the bottle in your hands, visualizing a red dragon coiling around it.
Chant over it and let it rest 3 days before use.
howToUse: Add a few drops to any other oil to boost its strength, dress red candles for power and protection, anoint charms and wands, or wear over the solar plexus when you need to stand in your strength.

description: A gentle spiritual healing oil for recovery of body and spirit, used alongside proper medical care. caution: External use only; never swallow, and keep it away from the eyes, the inside of the mouth and other mucous membranes. This blend is about 2.3% essential oil, suitable for occasional use on small areas of adult skin, so do not add extra drops; patch test on the inner forearm and wait 24 hours, stop if redness, itching or burning appears, and never apply it to broken or irritated skin. Avoid during pregnancy and breastfeeding unless cleared by a healthcare provider, do not use on infants or young children, and store the bottle out of reach of children and pets. Use only thyme linalool, not the harsher thymol type. When dressing candles, wipe excess oil from the wick and never leave a burning candle unattended.
pets: Essential oils can poison cats, dogs and birds if licked, absorbed or inhaled in a small space: never apply to pets, keep them from licking anointed skin or surfaces, and do not diffuse around cats or birds. This blend contains citrus oil, which is especially risky for cats.
